Many upstream inputs are not discussed here owing to limited supply chain information or relatively low importance (for inputs such as aluminum paste, argon, and nitric acid). 19 In August 2025, the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative extended the exclusions another three months to November 29, 2025. 24 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. • Silicon wafers: See Section 2.5. • Silver paste: Silver paste for screen-printing cell contacts typically contains silver powder, glass frit, and solvent (Zhao et al. 2024). Glass frit content is higher in front-side paste to create etching during firing (Thirsk 2011), and it is usually a PbO-based borosilicate glass (Fields et al. 2016). Interviews with industry in early 2025 indicated that silver and aluminum pastes must be imported from China or Southeast Asia. In 2024, U.S. silver demand was 30% for physical investment (bars), 29% for electronic and electrical applications, 12% for PV, 12% for jewelry and silverware, 6% for brazing and solder, and 7% for all other applications, including photography (U.S. Geological Survey 2025m). Industry interviews indicate that Dupont is establishing a U.S. supply of silver paste for c-Si PV module applications. • Process chemicals: Interviews with industry in early 2025 indicated that U.S. suppliers are generally used for process chemicals such as SiH , H , N , TMAl, POCl BBr , KOH, 4 2 2 3, 3 and HCl. Imports are unnecessary and can be hazardous to ship. However, raw precursors (e.g., KOH pellets or concentrated HCl) may be imported, and HF is generally imported. • Equipment: U.S. cell manufacturers report needing to import manufacturing equipment from China or Europe. European equipment was reported to have similar or slightly higher costs even if the 25% Section 301 tariffs on Chinese equipment were in effect. Cell patents affect the selection of manufacturing equipment (see Section 2.4.1). Cell manufacturers need access to variable material choices for each cell layer, different diffusion and deposition methods, and so forth to reduce litigation risk. Cell IP and equipment engineering and procurement issues are believed to be key vulnerabilities. Table 2 summarizes estimated costs for materials and equipment in the United States and Asia, and the availability of priority inputs for PERC cell production. The data shows cell materials costs in the United States are around 50% higher than cell materials costs within Asia, and equipment costs are closer to twice as high. Section 301 tariffs can account for 25% of the difference between metallization paste costs, while the rest of the difference is a combination of smaller scale for U.S. manufacturers, greater processing costs for U.S. suppliers, and possibly higher profit margins. 25 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications.
